notes: The detector diagnoses degeneracy but does not repair the estimator in the reported real-data tests.
Staged sensor blocking has multiple levels and an unblocked interval, but reports estimation rather than task outcomes.
Unknown static exploration is not MAP, and map uncertainty alone does not match a degradation source.
Terrain is deliberately selected; visual tracking failures are incidental because perceptual difficulty was not independently selected or varied.
CPU-only execution is a deliberately imposed single resource level; trajectory and timing measures are component outcomes.
The hardware comparison varies one versus three pedestrians but includes no zero-pedestrian level.
The fixed ten-second publishing schedule is a single imposed communication level; the located communication evaluation is replay.
D1 comes from simulated CSP and energy-budget levels; physical task evidence occurs under fixed difficult terrain and resource conditions.
The zero-delay setting retains other communication restrictions, so it is not a nominal COM control.
The update ablation is a with-and-without-response comparison under staged scene changes; missing depth and blur are incidental hardware observations.
Semantic grounding and long-range distance do not match a degradation source; the edge-server dependency was not varied or selected.
Moved targets are a one-level staged condition. Fixed onboard compute is addressed, and slow-inference failures are incidental rather than a varied budget.
Separately evaluated anomalous inputs and model misses establish selected learned-inference error, not navigation-task evidence.
All compared schedules remain energy-limited, so the original-period case is not a no-limit nominal control.
Previously occluded static obstacles and an unknown static map do not match MAP or DYN.
Incorrect observations map to SFA; deliberately incorrect prior-landmark poses map to MAP. Outcomes are estimator and map measures.
The route deliberately contains terrain and semantic traversability cases. Slow VLM response is handled but not varied as a condition.
The resource benchmarks models on its authors' recordings, so level_degradation is R rather than X.
Camera perturbation and clipped steering or damage are imposed without a same-system condition comparator; zero-shot embodiment tests are selected MOD evidence.
Unseen environments and goal-free exploration do not by themselves match MAP or MOD.
MAP is varied through zero and nonzero OSM deviations; GPS is disabled at one physical level. The campus sequence reports a physical task outcome.
Communication and computation are addressed, but no bandwidth cap is imposed and the evaluation assumes a connected graph.
Outdoor vegetation sites are deliberately selected difficult terrain rather than controlled terrain levels.
Different terrain scenes are D2. The heading penalty and cross-platform path differences show response feasibility depends on platform kinematics.
The card's model-error label is not MOD because no learned model is involved. Event-generator faults map to SFA; communication and computation are addressed but not varied as named conditions.
Illumination levels include normal and dark variants; compute platform is varied between PC and embedded hardware. Outcomes are component measures.
Cross-modal inputs and open-vocabulary localization do not by themselves establish PER, MAP, or MOD.
Compact sharing addresses bandwidth, but comparative simulations assume ideal connectivity and no link budget is imposed.
Communication series retain finite range or asymmetric failures, and robust ablations remain under outliers; no fully nominal source level was located.
Affordance modulation is the response comparator under the same stair and ramp conditions. The wheeled platform's inability to use stairs makes feasibility wheel-embodiment dependent.
Load scaling supplies D1 RES evidence, while physical tasks use one fixed resource-constrained configuration, producing a D2 conjunction. Network fallback is not induced.
Transition scenes are selected for low texture and tracking difficulty. The physical robot is teleoperated for path planning and obstacle avoidance.
The base policy and SELFI adaptation form a with-and-without-response comparison in organized pedestrian, uneven-floor, and learned-policy-error settings.
Frame rate is controlled across nonzero levels; seasonal outdoor sequences are deliberately selected rather than controlled recordings of one condition.
Repeated routes include daylight and controlled auxiliary-light intensities; visual errors remain component outcomes.
Numerical studies vary perfect versus imperfect observations and communication delay. Physical state-error traces are tracking measures, not mission-level outcomes.
Selection thresholds change produced traffic but no bandwidth cap or restricted link is imposed; COM is addressed but not named.
Simulation includes properly and poorly spaced maps; the selected vehicle run supplies stronger recorded-data evidence but only component outcomes.
Mission-gain versus base-controller comparisons occur under the same dynamic-agent and rough-terrain conditions; neither comparison removes the source.
